subtitle: Lesson 11 · Network Architecture at Enterprise Scale

eyebrow: Azure: a private zone, linked to a spoke
code:
az network private-dns zone create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --name internal.contoso.com

az network private-dns link vnet create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --zone-name internal.contoso.com \
  --name spoke-a-link \
  --virtual-network spoke-a-vnet \
  --registration-enabled false
caption: One zone in the hub, linked to every spoke that needs it — the link can cross subscriptions.

steps.label: Inbound endpoint
steps.sub: on-premises DNS servers query Azure private zones through a private IP

steps.label: Outbound endpoint + forwarding ruleset
steps.sub: Azure VMs forward specific domains out to on-premises DNS servers

steps.label: Result: one coherent resolution path, both directions
steps.sub: no hand-built IaaS DNS servers required

eyebrow: AWS: a private hosted zone, cross-account association
code:
aws route53 create-hosted-zone \
  --name internal.example.com \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 \
  --hosted-zone-config PrivateZone=true

aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone \
  --hosted-zone-id Z1D633PJN98FT9 \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0f1e2d3c4b5a69870
caption: Route 53 Resolver mirrors the Azure pattern: inbound endpoints, plus outbound endpoints and resolver rules.

steps.label: Per-spoke DNS: maximum autonomy, inconsistent by default
steps.sub: every team re-solves hybrid resolution independently, configs silently diverge

steps.label: Centralized DNS: one zone/resolver set, every spoke links in
steps.sub: same shared-services pattern the hub already provides for firewalling

steps.label: Tradeoff: nonstandard needs go through the central team
steps.sub: a guardrail, not a gate — the same tension Chapter 5 covers in depth

subtitle: Turning hub-and-spoke, hybrid connectivity, and centralized DNS into principles that hold as teams onboard.
